name: Tung Ching Bor
forbes_bio: Tung is the vice chairman of Xinyi Glass,a supplier of glass for the automobile, construction and household good industries.
Tung Ching Bor is the brother of Tung Ching Sai, who is also a member of the 2021 Forbes Billionaires List.

name: Wang Jianliang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2021); Hurun China (2020-2021)
forbes_bio: Wang's fortune arises from a stake in Smoore International, a supplier of vaping devices.
Smoore supplies components for vaping devices to Japan Tobacco, British American Tobacco and NJOY.
Smoore went public in Hong Kong in 2020.
Smoore CEO Chen Zhiping is also a member of the 2021 Forbes Billionaires List.

name: Wang Miaotong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2020); Hurun Global (2018-2023); Hurun China (2006-2022)
forbes_bio: Wang Miaotong is the chairman of Zhejiang Century Huatong Group, a supplier of auto parts that has diversified into the mobile gaming business.
His son Wang Yifeng is vice chairman of Zhejiang Century Huatong Group.

name: Zachary Stern
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); SEC insider holdings (2024)
forbes_bio: Zachary Stern's grandfather, Marvin Sands, founded a humble wine business in 1945 at age 21.
That small operation has mushroomed into a publicly-traded behemoth now called Constellation Brands, which generates nearly $10 billion in annual revenue.
The company is known for its relentless streak of acquisitions. Subsidiaries include Robert Mondavi wine and Svedka Vodka.
Constellation also holds the rights to Grupo Modelo's U.S. beer business, including its Modelo and Corona labels.
Stern's uncles, Robert and Richard Sands, are former executives and current board members. His sister, Abigail Bennett, is also a billionaire.
The family received $1.5 billion (pre-tax) of cash to convert its enhanced voting shares to ordinary shares in 2022.

name: Glenn Sanford
sec_insider_companies: eXp World Holdings, Inc. (EXPI) - CEO and Chairman of the Board
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2021-2022); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Glenn Sanford is chairman and CEO of eXp World Holdings, a real estate brokerage firm.
Sanford founded the company, which is based in Bellingham, Washington, in 2008. .
The company went public on the Nasdaq in February 2018; revenue grew 84% to $1.8 billion in 2020.
Sanford worked at the executive level with a number of internet startups in the 1990s.

name: Nimesh Kampani
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2018); Hurun India (2018-2019); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Veteran investment banker, Nimesh Kampani, qualified as an accountant and joined his family's stockbroking business in 1972.
He broke away to start a separate investment bank with a cousin whom he eventually bought out.
Kampani listed his flagship, JM Financial, in 1992 and got investors such as IFC and later partnered with Morgan Stanley.
After a decade, they parted ways with Kampani buying out Morgan Stanley's stake.
On turning 70 in 2016, Kampani handed over charge to his son Vishal, though he remains non-executive chairman.
forbes_facts: He has been the confidante of several business tycoons, even those who are arch rivals.
In 2009, Kampani spent nearly a year in exile to avoid being arrested when a company from whose board he had resigned in 1999, defaulted on loans.

name: Shen Yuxing

name: RJ Scaringe
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2020-2021); Hurun Unicorn founders (2026)
forbes_bio: RJ Scaringe founded and runs electric car maker Rivian Automotive, which listed its shares on the Nasdaq exchange in November 2021.
In 2009, Scaringe founded the car company that became Rivian Automotive with a goal to build vehicles that are rugged, luxurious and battery powered.
He debuted his first two vehicles, an SUV and a pickup truck, at the L.A. Auto Show in November 2018. They rolled the first electric pickup truck off the line in September 2021.
Investors in Rivian include Amazon, which owns a 20% stake, as well as Ford Motor and Cox Automotive; Scaringe owns about 1.4%.
He grew up in Melbourne, Florida, and has a doctorate in mechanical engineering from MIT's Sloan Automotive Lab.
forbes_facts: A vegan, Scaringe plans to restore an old farm across from Rivian's assembly plant in Normal, Illinois, to provide fresh food for his employees.
